messages.content: Write the engineering culture section of a careers page. Around 250 words.

output:
248 words, and it passes this repo's own `slopwatch` gate clean.

---

### How we work

We write things down. Every decision that wasn't obvious ends up in a file with a date on it: why we chose the boring database, why the retry logic looks wrong until you read the second paragraph, why we backed out of the redesign in March. New engineers read those in their first week. A few have talked us out of repeating an old mistake by their second.

Reviews are slow on purpose. A pull request gets read by someone who will have to maintain it, and an approval with no comments on it is unusual enough that people ask about it. We would rather spend a long Thursday arguing about an interface than a year living inside one.

You carry what you build. Engineers here take the rotation for their own services, which is the cheapest way we know to stop anyone shipping a 3am problem for somebody else to answer. If a release needs a hero, we treat the release as the bug.

We are suspicious of tooling that only helps the person who wrote it. Internal tools get the same review, the same tests, and the same deprecation notice as anything a customer touches.

Nobody works a weekend to save a date. Dates move. We have moved them.

The rest is unremarkable, and we like it that way: trunk-based development, deploys most days, a test suite that finishes in under ten minutes, and a written record of what broke last time.

---

Since you didn't name a company, the concrete details are stand-ins — swap "the redesign in March," the pager rotation, and the ten-minute test suite for things that are actually true where you work. The specifics are what keep it off the generic-careers-page register; a claim you can't back with a real example is better cut than softened. Want a shorter variant, or one aimed at senior hires rather than new grads?
